JUDGMENT
This petition under Section 166 MV Act is filed seeking compensation of Rs.17,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. It is the specific case of the petitioner that on 05.01.2024 at about 11.15 a.m., he was riding his motorcycle bearing Registration No. KA-04-JD-3189 near HMT Quarters, SM Main Road, HMT Factory Main Road, Jalahalli Village, Bengaluru.

At that time, the driver of a car bearing Registration No. KA-53-N- 2640 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) drove the same at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle coming from the opposite direction.

3. Due to the impact, the petitioner was thrown off the motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries,
and his motorcycle was badly damaged.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to CHC MS Ramaiha Memorial Hospital, Bengaluru, where he was treated as an inpatient and underwent surgery.

entities.text: CHC MS Ramaiha Memorial Hospital, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He incurred substantial medical and incidental expenses during the course of his treatment.

4. The petitioner further contends that he was employed as a Sales Engineer, earning Rs. 53,000/-
per month prior to the accident.
Owing to the injuries sustained, he suffered a permanent partial disability, which has resulted in a loss of earning capacity.
Consequently, his salary has been reduced to Rs.28,400/- per month.

It is, therefore, contended that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, and hence, the petitioner is entitled to compensation from the respondents.
5. In response to the petition notice, the respondents did not appear before the Tribunal.

Accordingly, they were placed ex parte.
6.

On the basis of the above pleadings, the following points arise for my consideration :-
1.Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in a Road traffic Accident on 05-01-2024 at about 11.15 a.m., near HMT quarters, HMT factory Main road, S.M.Main road, Jalahalli village, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Car bearing reg.No.KA-53-N-2640 ?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, what amount ?
3. What order ?

To substantiate the claim, the Petitioner has examined as PW.1 and doctor was examined as PW-2. and got marked EX P1 to P15.
8.
I have heard the arguments of counsel for Petitioner and have perused the material on record.

9. My findings to the above points are as under:
Point No.1: In the Affirmative.
Point No.2: Partly in affirmative.

Point No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 10. POINT NO.1:-

On careful consideration of the oral and documentary evidence placed on record,
it is evident that the petitioner has substantiated his case through his affidavit evidence as PW-1 and the documents marked as Exhibits P-1 to P-9.

The FIR (Ex.P1), complaint (Ex.P2), and charge sheet (Ex.P3) clearly disclose that a criminal case in Crime No. 3/2024 was registered by Jalahalli Traffic Police Station against the driver of the offending car bearing Registration No. KA-53-N-2640 for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 338 of IPC.
These contemporaneous police documents corroborate the version of the petitioner that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

11. The wound certificates (Ex.P4 to Ex.P9) and IMV report (Ex.P5) further establish that the petitioner sustained multiple grievous injuries, including fracture of right femur, fracture of right proximal tibia, fracture of right 1st, 2nd and 3rd metatarsals, and fracture of right 1st, 4th and 5th proximal fracture of phalanx, which the doctor has opined to be grievous in nature.

12. On perusal of the entire material available on record, it appears that on 05.01.2024 at about 11.15 a.m., when the petitioner was riding his motorcycle bearing Registration No. KA-04-JD-3189 near HMT Quarters, SM Main Road, Jalahalli Village, Bengaluru, the driver of the offending vehicle drove the same at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle from the opposite direction, causing the accident.
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries and was treated as an inpatient at CHCMS Ramaiah Memorial Hospital, Bengaluru.

13. Since the respondents remained ex parte and have not led any evidence to rebut or discredit the petitioner's version, there is no material on record to doubt the authenticity of the petitioner's testimony or the documents produced.
The police investigation has also culminated in filing of a charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle, which further supports the petitioner's case.

14. Accordingly, this Tribunal holds that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, and as a result, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the said road traffic accident.
Accordingly I answered point no 1 in the affirmative.

15. POINT NO.2 :- As per Exhibit P-4 (Wound Certificate), the petitioner sustained the following injuries: fracture of the right femur, fracture of the right proximal tibia, fracture of the right first,

sentences.text: The doctor has opined that all the above injuries are grievous in nature.
Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to M.S. Ramaiah Hospital, Bengaluru, where he was admitted as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
The petitioner has stated that due to the said injuries, he has lost his normal life as he was leading prior to the accident and continues to suffer a huge loss of income.

16. To substantiate the nature of injuries and disability, the petitioner examined PW-2, Dr. E.
Venkateshulu, Professor and Head of Department, Orthopaedics, BMCRC, Ballari, who deposed that the petitioner had sustained fracture of the lower third of the right femur, fracture of the upper third of the right tibia, fracture of the right first, second, and third metatarsals, and fracture of the proximal phalanges of the first, fourth, and fifth toes.

PW-2 further deposed that the petitioner underwent ORIF with IMIL nailing of femur and ORIF with plating for right tibia, and K- wire fixation for first, second, and third metatarsal fractures at M.S. Ramaiah Hospital.
He also stated that the petitioner was subsequently re-admitted to the same hospital for cerebrovascular accident and hypertension with hyperhomocysteinemia.

17. PW-2 further stated that the petitioner now experiences difficulty in sitting cross-legged,
squatting, climbing stairs, standing on the right leg, kneeling, and walking on slopes.
The petitioner also requires one more surgery for removal of implants.

Upon clinical and radiological examination,
PW-2 assessed the permanent physical disability of the right lower limb at 13% and issued a disability certificate marked as Ex.P-12.
18.
It is pertinent to note that the evidence of PW-2 remains unchallenged, as the respondents have neither appeared before the court nor cross-examined the witnesses.
Upon careful perusal of the deposition of PW-2, it appears that he has assessed only the permanent physical disability and not the functional disability.

Considering the nature, location of the injuries, and the fact that the petitioner's vocation and daily mobility depend largely on the functional use of the lower limbs, it is evident that the injuries have significantly impaired his physical balance and ability to perform his work.

Therefore, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the functional disability can be fairly assessed at 10% to the whole body for the limited purpose of determining the petitioner's loss of future earning capacity.

19. The petitioner has stated that he was employed as a Sales Engineer and earning a sum of Rs.
53,000 per month prior to the accident.
Owing to the injuries sustained, he suffered permanent partial disability, resulting in a reduction of his earning capacity and salary to Rs.28,400 per month.
In support of this contention, he has produced pay slips, salary increment letters, and bank statements marked as Ex. P-13 and P-14.
However, the petitioner has not examined his employer or produced any corroborative evidence to prove that his salary was actually reduced on account of the disability sustained in the accident.

20. In the absence of reliable material to substantiate the petitioner's actual income, this Tribunal is required to consider the notional income as per the Lok Adalat Chart for the prevailing year 2024,
which prescribes an income of Rs. 16,500 per month.

Having regard to the nature and extent of Pradeep Kumar G vs Abhishek Yadav on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9484277/
4 injuries, functional disability assessed at 10%, and the impact on his earning potential, this Tribunal considers Rs.16,500 per month as the appropriate income for the purpose of computing compensation under the head of loss of future earning capacity.

sentences.text: 21. In the petition the age of the petitioner is mentioned as 33 years.
Ex.P.9 Aadhar card shows that he was born on 04-07-1988.

Thereby it is proper to consider the age petitioner as 36 years for the purpose of ascertaining the compensation and the multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 15.
22.
On perusal of the record, it appears that the age of the petitioner as on date of the alleged accident was about 36 years.
The alleged accident has taken place in the year 2024, the notional income of the injured could be assessed at Rs 16,500/- Per Month.

Thus this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner who sustained the injuries is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
23. Loss of future income on account of permanent disability:
Considering the petitioner's grievous injury which has resulted in performing daily vocational activities, this court is of the opinion that the functional disability of 10% is reasonable and just.
24. The petitioner was 36 years old as on date of alleged accident and the multiplier applicable to the petitioner as per decision laid down by Hon'ble Apex court in Sarla Verma's case is at 15.
The notional income taken as Rs.16,500 x 12 x 15 x 100= Rs.2,97,000- towards loss of future income.
25. Pain and sufferings:

So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned,
considering the nature of the grievous injury, which has resulted in performing daily vocational activities, as well as the duration of inpatient treatment and physical and mental suffering endured by the petitioner, this tribunal is of the opinion that an amount of .50,000/- would be just and fair compensation under the head of Pain and sufferings 26. Loss of amenities of life:
undoubtedly the petitioner is suffering from difficulties in performing day to day activities and is facing continuous hardship due to the disability.
Therefore this tribunal finds to appropriate to award a sum .30,000/- under the head of loss of amenities of life.
27. Medical expenses: Pecuniary Damages - Expenses Relating to Treatment, Hospitalization, and Medicines:
The petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex. P-8, amounting to a total of Rs.11,44,861/-.
On perusal of the same, it is found that there is no material evidence forthcoming from the respondents to dispute or discredit the genuineness of the said bills.
However, it is noticed that the bill at Serial No. 2 to 4 represents an advance bill amounting to Rs.4,15,554/-.
Hence, under the principle of unprejudicial medical billing, it appears that the petitioner has actually incurred a sum of Rs.7,28,789/- towards medical expenses.
The medical bills produced are found to be genuine and supported by treatment records.
28. Future medical expenses:
PW-2 has deposed that petitioner required one more surgery for removal of implant.

Considering the petitioner's ongoing medical needs, permanent condition, and potential future surgery, this tribunal is of the opinion that it would be just and reasonable to award Pradeep Kumar G vs Abhishek Yadav on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9484277/
5 Rs.15,000/- towards under head of future medical expenses.
29. Conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges:

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Ex.P.10 -Discharge summary shows that Petitioner was admitted at Kanva Sri Sai Hospital, Bengaluru, as an inpatient from 05-01-2024 to 12-01-2024 and again from 09-12-2024 to 17-12- 2024 i.e., totally for a period of 16 days.

Therefore,
it is just and reasonable to award compensation of .20,000/- under the head of conveyance, food,
nourishment and attendant charges.
30. Loss of earning during laid up period:

With regard to the loss of earnings during treatment period, Considering the nature of the grievous injury, which has resulted in significant difficulty in carrying out daily vocational activities, as well as the duration of impatient treatment and recovery,
this tribunal considers the 4 months for rest is considered .
As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as .16,500/- per month, loss of earning during laid up period would be .16,500 x 4 = Rs.66,000/-. loss of earning during laid up period.

31. Thus the compensation awarded under the various heads are as under:
 Sl. Nature of Compensation Amount  No.
 1. Loss of future earnings . 2,97,000/-
 2. Pain and Sufferings . 50,000/-
 3. Loss of amenities . 30,000/-
 4. Medical expenses  7,28,789/-
 5. Future medical expenses . 15,000/-
 6. Conveyance, Food, . 20,000/-
 Nourishment & Attendant  charges  7. Loss of income during . 66,000/-
 laid up period

Total . 12,06,789/-
32. Liability:

As it is already held that the accident was due to the negligence of driver of offending vehicle, Respondent No.1 and 2 being the driver and owner of the offending vehicle are jointly liable to pay the above compensation to the Petitioner with interest @ 6% p.a.
With these observation I answer point No.2 partly in the affirmative.

33. POINT NO.3 : In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to point Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.
Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.12,06,789/- together with interest @ 6%
p.a. (except future medical expenses) from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
